 Common Judgment

These two petitions are brought U/Sec.166 of
M.V. Act 1988 for the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/
and Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the
petitioner and for the death of Sri.P.Venki Rao, in the
road traffic accident caused on 27.12.2022.

02 . Hence these two petitions were clubbed
together for the purpose of recording common
evidence.

The main petition is M.V.C.No.630/2023 and
it is clubbed with M.V.C.No.2171/2023.
 03.

The brief facts in M.V.C.No.630/2023 are
as under:

It is submitted that on 27.12.2022 at about
04.00 a.m., when the deceased namely P.Venki Rao
was driving the goods carrier vehicle bearing No.
Ka08A1346 from Rayachoty towards Madanapalle

As a result the

suffered severe injuries.

Then he was shifted to

But

 a) Ilr 2016 Kar 55 - M/s Icici Lombard Gic

The Karnataka State Road
Transportation Corporation - It is observed that the
tribunal on basis of evidence on record has to decide
whether there is contributory negligence or not.

The
tribunal has to find out the contributory negligence
from the sketch drawn by the concerned police.

c) Ilr 2009 Kar 385 - Smt.Nasreen Banu and
others V/s The Divisional Manager and another - It is
observed that the negligence of offending vehicle need
not be established beyond reasonable doubt like that
of penal action case.

One cannot loose sight of
Evidence Act and in civil case it is purely based on

Therefore, in my opinion there is no material

 Order
The claim petition filed by the petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/2023 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is
hereby allowed in part, with costs.
The petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/2023 are entitled for Rs.30,26,864/ (T
hirty lakhs twenty six thousand eight hundred and sixty four only) compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However in view of holding valid policy the respondent No.2 shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for 40% each and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for 20% of the award amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There are no
supportive documents on behalf of the respondent
No.2 to show that their bus driver was not at fault.
Even there are no documents to show that the
accident occurred due to the negligence of the goods
vehicle driver/deceased.
So on perusal of these documents it is
true that the petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/23 are the
parents and sister of the deceased and they have to be
considered as legal heirs and dependents of the
deceased.
Hence from the above documents and in
absence of any other supportive documents on behalf
of the respondents, I am of opinion that the bus driver
had caused accident to the petitioner and to the son of
petitioner No.1 and they have sustained injuries.
c) Ilr 2009 Kar 385 - Smt.Nasreen Banu and
others V/s The Divisional Manager and another - It is
observed that the negligence of offending vehicle need
not be established beyond reasonable doubt like that
of penal action case.
. The date of accident was in the year
2022.
Under these circumstances it is just and proper
to consider the Minimum Wages Act by considering the
 (Scch3) 16 MVC.No.630/23 c/w
 MVC.No.2171/23
deceased as semi skilled job as he was working as
driver which comes to Rs.14,469/ per month.
Since the deceased has left three dependents, as
per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport
Corporation and others case reported in 2009 Acj
1298 if the dependents are 2 to 3, then personal
deduction is to be 1/3rd.
Hence, in this case 1/3rd
deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.
So, after deduction of 1/3rd (Rs.4,823/), then the
income comes to Rs.9,646/.
As per
Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla
Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation
and others case reported in 2009 Acj 1298 the
petitioners are entitled for future prospects.
Since it is settled law in National Insurance
Company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in
Air 2017 Sc 5157 that the dependents would be
entitled for loss of estate to the extent of
Rs.15,000/ and funeral expenses to the extent of
Rs.15,000/, as such I award the same.
No.1 and 2 being the parents of the
Bhanu Prasad.
But the petitioner No.3 being the
sister who is under care and custody of the petitioner
No.1 is not entitled for any future prospects as per
Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India
Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder
Kaur & Ors case and Magma General Insurance
Company case in (2018) 18 Scc 130.
